analysis.investment_thesis: EPW India is a genuine fast-grower — revenue exploded from ₹7 Cr to ₹53 Cr in two years (~175% CAGR) in the underpenetrated refurbished electronics space, and at P/E 31x the PEG is optically compelling. However, the business burned ₹11 Cr in operating cash flow in FY25 despite reporting ₹4 Cr profit, which is a serious earnings quality red flag that must resolve before this becomes a conviction buy.
key_strengths: Explosive revenue growth: 7→19→53 Cr (FY23-25), a genuine fast-grower story Lynch could understand from a consumer angle — affordable refurbished laptops/Chromebooks in India.
ROCE of 65.7% and improving margins (EBITDA ₹6 Cr on ₹53 Cr revenue = ~11%) show the underlying unit economics are real.
P/E 31x on a company growing earnings 4x in one year gives a PEG well below 1.0 if growth even partially sustains.
key_risks: Severe cash flow divergence: ₹4 Cr net profit but -₹11 Cr operating cash flow in FY25 — the working capital model is broken or earnings are low quality.
Debt jumped from ₹0 to ₹12 Cr in a single year (D/E 2.4x) purely to fund working capital; this growth is being borrowed, not earned.
Micro-cap (₹129 Cr mkt cap, ₹53 Cr revenue) with zero analyst coverage — subject to operator activity and low liquidity risk.
red_flags: Operating CF deeply negative (-₹11 Cr) despite ₹4 Cr reported profit — classic sign of aggressive revenue recognition or working capital deterioration in a distribution business.
D/E ratio of 2.4x far exceeds my 0.6 comfort threshold; this is a leverage-funded growth story, not organic cash generation.
Total equity only ₹5 Cr — the high ROE (139%) is a mathematical artifact of near-zero equity base, not genuine capital efficiency.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
EPW India fits Lynch's 'fast grower' archetype on the surface — a simple, understandable business (refurbished electronics for price-sensitive Indian consumers) growing revenues 7.5x in two years in a large TAM. The P/E of 31x against this growth rate gives a sub-0.2 PEG, which would normally be screaming buy territory. ROCE of 65.7% and an improving EBITDA margin suggest the core model has pricing power. Promoter holding at 71% signals alignment, and FII/DII combined at 13.5% shows institutional validation at this micro-cap level.

The cash flow statement kills the story for now. A company with ₹4 Cr net profit posting -₹11 Cr operating cash flow means either receivables/inventory are exploding (dangerous in refurbished electronics where obsolescence is rapid) or the revenue is being stuffed into the channel. The ₹12 Cr borrowing in one year to fund this gap is exactly what Lynch warns about — when a company has to borrow to fund working capital as it grows, the growth machine has a leak. I would need two quarters of positive OCF conversion and debt reduction before upgrading to BUY. Watch the FY26 numbers closely — if cash flow turns, this re-rates sharply.
